title: X Feed Digest
summary: Gemini 3 Deep Think got a major upgrade (sketch→3D workflows) and posted a huge Codeforces jump, underscoring rapid reasoning gains.
Agent tooling matured: Anthropic’s Skills guide plus new memory systems (Context Repositories) and data/doc tools (Reader, DeepWiki) push practical automation.
Semiconductor signals strengthened as Applied Materials guided well above expectations, a leading indicator for the AI hardware cycle.
AI infrastructure is colliding with energy policy: Anthropic will cover grid‑upgrade costs tied to its data centers to avoid shifting burdens to ratepayers.
Geopolitical and industry tensions rose with Musk/OpenAI/Anthropic public clashes and Taiwan pressing a $40B defense bill.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Gemini 3 Deep Think upgrade
items.body: Google released a major upgrade to Gemini 3 Deep Think, targeting practical research/engineering workflows. It can interpret sketches and output 3D‑printable models; rollout is live for AI Ultra subscribers.

items.title: @deedydas: Gemini 3 Deep Think Codeforces jump
items.body: A benchmark report claims Gemini 3 Deep Think hit 3455 on Codeforces (~#8 human), far above the prior AI best (OpenAI o3 at 2727), signaling a big leap in competitive‑programming reasoning.

items.title: @akshay_pachaar: Anthropic Skills guide
items.body: Anthropic published a 33‑page guide to building Skills—packaged, repeatable workflows for Claude/agents—with concrete patterns (orchestration, tool selection, refinement) and common pitfalls.

items.title: @GitHub_Daily: Reader LLM web‑scraping engine
items.body: Highlights Reader, an open‑source web‑scraping engine built for LLM pipelines that handles anti‑bot hurdles and outputs clean Markdown; ships with CLI/API and Docker‑ready deployment.

items.title: @wang_xiaolou: DeepWiki turns repos into docs
items.body: DeepWiki auto‑generates a wiki for any GitHub repo by swapping .com → .pm, producing architecture diagrams, module analysis, and AI Q&A to speed up codebase understanding.

items.title: @shao__meng: Letta Context Repositories
items.body: Letta announced “Context Repositories” that store agent memory as local files with Git versioning, enabling auditability, branching/merging, and multi‑agent memory workflows.

items.title: @ReyezAriel: AMAT guidance beats
items.body: Applied Materials guided next‑quarter revenue to ~$7.65B and EPS ~$2.64, both well above expectations; the post argues AMAT orders lead the AI‑semiconductor cycle and signal HBM capacity expansion in 6–12 months.

items.title: @AnthropicAI: Data‑center grid costs
items.body: Anthropic says it will cover 100% of grid‑upgrade costs and power‑price increases tied to its data centers, aiming to avoid shifting costs to ratepayers and reduce grid strain.

items.title: @KKaWSB: AI giants clash publicly
items.body: Notes an escalating public dispute: Musk suing OpenAI and calling out Anthropic, with Anthropic responding—framing a shift from product competition to open positioning and narrative battles.

items.title: @DominoTheoryMag: Taiwan $40B defense bill
items.body: Reports Taiwan’s President Lai urging opposition lawmakers to pass a $40B defense bill immediately, warning delays could weaken security and global confidence.

items.title: @adxtyahq: NASA’s C coding rules
items.body: JPL’s mission‑critical C rules ban recursion and post‑init allocations, require bounded loops and assertions, and enforce zero warnings with daily static analysis—showing how extreme reliability constraints shape code style.

items.title: @pangyusio: Project‑driven learning
items.body: Argues that focused, project‑driven learning can make someone job‑ready in ~6–12 months in the AI era, while long traditional pipelines waste time and miss the opportunity window.

items.title: @plantegg: Let AI write your README
items.body: Tip: after finishing a task, ask AI to summarize steps and pitfalls into a README so future you (or another model) can pick up the work quickly—lightweight long‑term memory across tools.
